title: Spikes's view of Jelly Roll Morton's personality
summary: Jelly Roll was sincere but foolish, thinking everyone stole his jazz and wanting to sue ASCAP and Duke Ellington.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Tell me more about Jelly Roll.

[Chuckles] Well, what do you want to know about Jelly Roll? He was a...I don't know...Jelly Roll was a...aww, he was sincere about what he said, but everything he said was so foolish. He tried...I think he tried to sue ASCAP because he thought they was stealing his stuff. He tried...wanted to sue everybody that played any jazz or anything he said is stealing from them, and he wanted to sue them and everything. [Laughs] He think he started all of that. He thinks he started all of that and everybody that played. I think he was going to try to sue Duke Ellington if I ain't mistaken or something...talking about it anyway. But he...everybody that he'd hear play anything jazz, he'd say, "That's mine. He stole that from me. He stole it." But he was a nice guy but he was just...think everybody in the world that was playing anything like jazz was of his stuff, you know. And he died, you know. He came back here about '38 and he died, and then I opened...I opened the...'38...no, '38...no,
*Ed's. note: Morton died July 10, 1941 in Los Angeles, California.
